examples.knowledge_point: Solving an Inequality Involving Exponential Functions with Different Exponents and a Polynomial
examples.worked_solution:
First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{5}\cdot {4}^{x} & >{4}^{x-15} \\ {x}^{5}\cdot {4}^{x}-{4}^{x-15} & >0 \\ ({x}^{5}-{4}^{-15})\cdot {4}^{x} & >0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by $4^{x}$ and get

$$
x^5 - 4^{-15} > 0.
$$

Finally, we can solve this inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{5} & >{4}^{-15} \\ \sqrt[5]{{x}^{5}} & >\sqrt[5]{{4}^{-15}} \\ x & >{({4}^{-15})}^{1/5} \\ x & >{4}^{-3} \\ x & >\frac{1}{64}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality is $x > \dfrac{1}{64}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{2}^{2x-3}{x}^{2}+3x\cdot {2}^{2x-3} & >-4\cdot {2}^{2x-3} \\ (-{x}^{2}+3x+4){2}^{2x-3} & >0 \\ -({x}^{2}-3x-4){2}^{2x-3} & >0 \\ -(x+1)(x-4){2}^{2x-3} & >0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${2}^{2x-3}$ and get

$$
-(x+1)(x-4)>0.
$$

This represents a downwards parabola whose roots are at $x=-1$ and $x=4.$ The parabola is above the $x$-axis when $-1<x<4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013930/assets/df6c1c0ac26d9074f8c726b2265780fefad631561d7a729d2dfc7998ef043859.png)

Therefore, the solution is $-1<x<4.$
